videos.t: esp32 relays and solenoids          #esp32 #arduino #pcb
videos.desc:
My first custom relay boards using ESPNow

I am doing a somewhat ambitious art project where I need 1 master esp32 and 6 slave esp32s controlling 2 relays each for a 12V load.

The wiring got ugly and i decided designing a pcb would be faster and prettier than soldering up 6 proto-boards.

It's pretty awesome how gpt4 told me the model numbers for appropriate transistors, flyback diodes, and base resistors (I have never done a project with non-LED diodes, transistors, or bare relays).

Wireless Fire: ESPNow and Propane
videos.desc:
I want my idyllic suburbanite life to be more awesome. More badass. So I decided to make walkway lights, only they're not walkway lights… they are propane cannisters automated with solenoid valves, high voltage arc generators, and esp32 microcontrollers running the ESPNow library, allowing them to establish a local network that, well, uses relays to let me tell them when and how to shoot fire in my front yard.

Defintely check out my buddy Tomasz if you have not yet: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2c-yxTgw7Eo&t=78s

videos.desc: This project uses the Ibus  serial protocol from a Flysky RC receiver.  That stream  is read by an ESP32 over a second uart port, parsed,  and converted into meaningful data from the RC transmitter. That data  is then used to control two BTS7960  motor drivers for the wheels and a 35kg * cm  servo on the steering wheel.

videos.desc: Little Timmy is just a skeleton with a pan tilt head, an FPV camera for an eye, and propane that shoots out of his skull when he's excited. Much like Pinocchio, my latest long-term project is to turn him into a real boy. Openai Faster-whisper? Check. Piper TTS? Check. Now I just need to customize a voice, preferably sounding like skeleton, a large language model to give him some personality, and an API to allow guest hosts to possess him. ￼

videos.t: Piper TTS training a model to sound like Skeletor
videos.desc:
I am using Piper TTS to finetune the lgspeech model to sound like Skeletor, from He-Man. My co-host, little Timmy, needs a voice. I couldn't find enough clean audio of Skeletor from the cartoon, so i had to improvise. This is an impromptu vid of me reading 142 different phrases, trying to sound like Skeletor.



#piper #whisper #openai #ollama #faster-whisper #homeassistant #pipertts #tts #raspi #raspi5 #voicerecognition #voicecloning #python #wsl

videos.t: Making Timmy a real boy#TTS #ollama #piper #robotics #raspi #openai #voicecloning #metallica #python
videos.desc:
I will turn the skeleton from my last project into a cohost. Openai Faster-whisper does speech to text. That gets piped to a locally hosted LLM using ollama. The output uses Piper TTS. Cap for testing, as is seen here, I can let a friend remotely "possess" Timmy to control his head pan tilt servos, see-through his eye (using H.264HLS streaming), and enter text commands into a flask python server better than red allowed by Piper.

Very simple straightforward project.

videos.t: Voice cloning Skeletor #esp32 #raspi #piper #STT #ghostrider #servoskull
videos.desc: I am running a python package called Piper honey raspberry pi 5 that does a great job with text to speech, and it also allows you to use different voice models (.onnx files). It's really impressive. I couldn't find enough clean audio of just Skeletor talking, so I used an open source fine-tuning voice model package to record 142 entries of me reading sentences of predetermined text. I read them like Skeletor. This was the output. ￼

videos.t: This is a #raspi running #piper TTS #voicecloning #skeletor singing #snoopdogg #maker #python
videos.desc: This is part of operation Pinocchio, turning my take on ghost rider in my daughter's power wheels into a real boy. I am taking an existing cast-iron skull on a pant access that is RC and esp32 controlled that shoots propane from a previous project. I am making the jaw articulate.
I use #Pipe text-to-speech to read and put text from a web server, then immediately speak that text using a custom fine tuned neural network voice model that I made to sound like skeleton.

videos.t: I will turn Timmy into a real boy. #robotics #piper #tts #openai #oll￼ama #llm #homeassistant #agent
videos.desc:
In a previous video, I made a propane igniting Pediatric skeleton drive my daughters power wheels using radio control, and ESP 32, an FPV camera, and a pan/tilt servo system.

Now, that skeleton is named little Timmy, and he lives in my workshop. He is my cohost, foil, and helper.  Entirely locally run, I use faster-whisper for speech-to-text, his brain is a locally run llm with my custom pre-processing (including short term, episodic, and semantic memory), and his speech uses the piper python package with a fine tune model to sound like my imitation of Skeletor. 

It's going well.  ￼

videos.desc:
Little Timmy was a pan tilt RC controlled POV skeleton head with an FPV camera in him last Halloween. He drove a Barbie power wheels that was also RC controlled through an ESP 32 intermediary between the receiver and the actuators.

I didn't know what to do with him, so I thought it would be easy to make him hear, talk, think, learn, stream low latency video, summarize images, perform both face identification and recognition, and some other stuff.

I did all of the above stuff, now I just need to restore his ability to create fire from his skull￼, then I can finally unleash him as my cohost. ￼

videos.t: My wood-burning stove heats my shop with a raspberry pi and a car radiator.
videos.desc: It's basically a giant solar stove, with insulation and a smoke stack on top, made out of two 55 gallon drum drums, with some copper coil going through it, then the water gets hot and goes through a variety of solenoid valves to ensure complete safety, then goes to a radiator off an old Nissan, then back to the heater. The temperature gets measured at six points. It gets graphed and saved. Kept currently figuring out the actual heat dissipation properties of the system so I can fine-tune it and make it run automatically. #offgrid #controlsystems #raspi #solenoid #diy #thermodynamics #woodburni

videos.t: Predator Gimbal, 80's, depth perception, edge motion tracking, object detention, oak-d
videos.desc:
This project uses a Luckfox Rockchip Omni rk3576 board that I snagged, and an OAK-D Lite stereoscopic embedded AI camera I snagged.

The plan is to use my existing implementation of simplefoc arduino/esp32 to control a three axis gimbal that houses the camera, add two IMU's, then sync the camera to my head. Only I will be able to make it locked on the target. A moving target. Or still target while I move.


I want a predator gimbal. I need one. I want a shoulder mounted device that aims where my head is aiming. It could be great. School talent shows. Family gatherings. Locking target on nemesi
